title: Expert review analysis
description: Returned by each book-guided expert to the coordinator in architecture-review.

book_practices.description: One entry for every selected book, tracing its practices to architecture evidence and review output.

book_id.description: Exact id from this expert's selected book list.

title.description: Exact title from the selected book list.

edition.description: Exact edition from the selected book list.

knowledge_basis.description: The expert used its pretrained knowledge; this is not a claim about exact training-set membership.

chapters_used.description: Distinct chapters recalled and used. Every chapter must contribute at least one applied practice.

chapter.description: Exact chapter number and title recalled for this edition.

sections.description: Exact section names recalled and used from this chapter.

practice.description: A named principle or practice specifically associated with this chapter or its listed sections.

interpretation.description: What the practice means in the expert's own words.

architecture_evidence.description: The concrete code, design, constraint, or artifact examined through this practice.

applied_to.description: The exact finding, upheld practice, or recommendation shaped by this practice.

application.description: How applying the practice to the evidence produced or supported that review judgment.

assessment_note.description: Optional one-line nuance, e.g. aligned on preserved behavior, at_risk on the new surface.

practice.description: Concrete choice worth preserving that a future change could plausibly regress; praise without evidence is dropped.

severity.description: P0: demonstrated main-path failure, data loss, or security break — blocks release. P1: a concrete failure scenario that a user, an operator, or the next dependent change will plausibly hit. P2: a real cost that accumulates (latent defect, performance, maintenance) with no near-term failure path. P3: small but real and cheap to fix. The risk field alone must justify the grade.

claim.description: One-sentence statement of the gap or risk.

risk.description: Concrete failure, security, compatibility, performance, operational, or maintenance cost.

recommendations.description: Structural or panel-level improvements beyond any single finding; each finding's smallest_fix already covers itself.

standards_conformance.description: Required from the AI architect (role ai). One entry per artifact and standard pair for agent skills, plugins, MCP servers or clients, and agent instruction files in scope; a single not_applicable entry when the scope has none.

artifact.description: The skill, plugin, MCP server or client, or instruction file checked, by path or name.

clause.description: The section or rule of the standard that was checked.

evidence.description: What in the artifact shows the verdict; for not_applicable, why no such artifact is in scope.

assumptions.description: Missing facts that could change the assessment.
